bull.b: Ten consecutive quarters of year-over-year growth indicate sustained product adoption rather than a single-period increase. Continued expansion in revenue and six-month sales can improve operating leverage, support broader distribution, and strengthen SKYX’s position in building and renovation markets over coming quarters.

The pipeline spans hotels, builders, retail, and international projects, giving SKYX multiple routes to scale its platform. If phased deployments convert as planned, larger volumes could broaden market penetration, deepen channel relationships, and create a more durable base for future product sales.

The substantially stronger cash position and lower quarterly cash burn improve near-term financial flexibility while management works toward positive cash flow. Debt reduction also modestly lowers financing pressure, allowing more capacity to support commercialization and product expansion than at year-end 2025.

bear.b: Stable gross margins have not yet translated into operating or net profitability, showing that the current scale remains insufficient to cover the company’s cost base. Persistent losses can constrain reinvestment, increase dependence on external financing, and make earnings improvement heavily dependent on successful volume growth.

The business is still consuming cash rather than funding operations internally, even though quarterly burn has improved. Continued negative operating and free cash flow could limit strategic flexibility, require additional capital, and leave execution more sensitive to delays in deployments, approvals, or revenue conversion.

Meaningful debt relative to the equity base already limits financial flexibility, while the proposed Deako transaction adds cash-and-notes funding and completion uncertainty. Approval, closing, and integration issues could increase financing demands or delay the expected builder access, synergies, and platform expansion.
